gap: No result ChatGPT got states a lab-measured figure for the 15.6-inch screens it recommended: the ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK measured 140.2 nits (ServeTheHome) to 205 cd/m² (ITPro) against ASUS's 250 cd/m² rating with 62-68% sRGB, and the dual 15.6-inch UPERFECT Delta measured 226 cd/m² on its adapter but 160 cd/m² on a single USB-C cable (Notebookcheck).
standout_why: I opened the two cited pages (itechguides '15 Best', deskgearhq) and the two 15.6-inch pages from chat 1 (theofficejournal and workcocoon). None carries a reviewer-measured figure: itechguides uses maker and listing ratings only, deskgearhq names PCMag, RTINGS and Notebookcheck for general context while saying lab tests of its picks are limited, and the other two show only listing claims such as '85% sRGB'. Our own dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender (a result in chat 2) carries only Macworld's power notes on the Trio 3 Pro and Duex Float 2 Pro, and does not mention the MB169CK or the UPERFECT Delta. The limit on this angle is that I could open no named measurement for the FOPO S10 or the Duex Max DS, so it grades the rival picks, not ours.
decides: It does not change which of our screens wins, because no named lab has measured the FOPO S10 or Duex Max DS in anything I could open; their brightness and contrast must be labelled as the maker's ratings. It qualifies ChatGPT's two 15.6-inch rival picks: the MB169CK measured well under its 250 cd/m² rating and falls to 114 cd/m² when the laptop port under-powers it (ITPro), and the UPERFECT Delta loses about 29% of its brightness on one cable (Notebookcheck). Three separate tests (Notebookcheck on the Delta, ITPro on the MB169CK, Macworld on the Trio 3 Pro) found a laptop-powered screen short of full brightness, so the page should tell a 15.6-inch laptop owner to budget a wall adapter for any pick, dual-screen ones most of all.
